private_defaults_are_not_source_facts: channel_depth_mm and insertion_margin_mm: 0 = undeclared, absent from all retained sources
picket engagements: undeclared; a between_frame cut length without engagements is face-to-face only

rail placements are drawing-derived authored choices from the CAD section chain; datum unconfirmed
withheld_from_consumer_shape: all null receiving depths from the producer draft (stayed absent, never defaulted)
per-panel quantity Tokens (counts live in the dataset and the publication report, not the consumer model)

limitations: channel_depth, insertion_margin and engagement nulls are declared absences: no retained source states rail slot depth, picket seating depth or post rail-socket depth for this configuration.
Rail placement offsets are drawing-derived authored choices from the CAD section chain, not manufacturer-stated datums; the chain-to-opening datum interpretation is unconfirmed.
Picket qty is null in each run: the count follows from run length and installed pitch, neither of which is source-stated; it must not be filled with an invented default.
The model fragment authors no post opinion: a composition-only post Part carries no citable evidence values, and no source states Augusta post dimensions or SKU identity.

Rail placement offsets are CENTERLINES (consumer placement semantics); the 5.5in envelope halves to 69.85mm, which is exact in milli-mm but not in whole millimetres — the consumer conversion floors with a recorded loss.

Kit counts are manufacturer inventory statements, not installed-pitch derivations: the picket stock length 43in exceeds the 39.5in run by an implied 3.5in seating, which is config-dependent and still not a measured engagement.

Upper picket run (between mid_rail and top_rail): withheld from the consumer mapping under consumer_infill_single_cycle — the consumer infill fits one repeating cycle per panel, so two stacked rows between different rail pairs cannot be expressed without alternating across the width. Its two u-channel segments are withheld with it. Both runs remain recorded in the draft model_fragment and the dataset composition. See withheld_mappings.

Rail length rule: the sources state rails slide INTO routed post sockets, and the draft knows the 71.5in rail stock, but the consumer's routed-rail length path requires a PostSlot.receiving_joint (post socket depth), which no retained source states and this candidate does not author. clear_between_posts is therefore published as the registry rule the routed path extends — with NO invented socket engagement — and any future resolved cut length will undercount the known stock until a receiving joint is authored from real evidence.
This candidate is a diagnostic input for consumer validation, not the production route.
Consumer validation of this candidate does not admit any FenceModel to the published snapshot.

withheld_mappings.reason: the consumer infill fits one repeating member cycle per panel (fit.py: member_widths_mm[i % len(pattern)]); two stacked rows between different rail pairs cannot be expressed without alternating across the width
withheld_mappings.would_close: consumer support for per-row span derivation from each member's base_ref/top_ref, or a multi-row infill capability

withheld_mappings.reason: the upper run is withheld under consumer_infill_single_cycle, so its two u-channel segments (first and last picket above the mid rail) cannot be edge-bound to a mapped member
withheld_mappings.would_close: the same consumer multi-row infill capability that unblocks the upper run
